name: H-1B Specialty Occupation Visa
quickAnswer: The H-1B lets a U.S. employer temporarily hire a foreign professional for a specialty occupation that normally requires at least a bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in a specific field. Cap-subject filings are limited each year and often selected by lottery; employers must also obtain a certified Labor Condition Application before filing with USCIS.
whoIsFor: Professionals offered a specialty role that truly requires bachelor’s-level skills in a related field
Applicants with a qualifying degree or carefully documented equivalent experience
People with an employer willing to sponsor, pay required wages, and handle the petition
Candidates changing or extending status in the U.S., or applicants who will consular process abroad
whoShouldNotApply: Anyone without a real employer-sponsor for a specialty occupation
Roles that are routine, non-specialty, or only loosely related to your education
People seeking permanent work authorization as the sole purpose of this filing
Self-petitioners trying to work primarily for an unstructured personal venture
eligibility: The job must qualify as a specialty occupation — typically requiring a bachelor’s or higher in a specific specialty
You must hold the required degree (or equivalent education/experience) for that specialty
A U.S. employer must offer the role and pay at least the required wage for the worksite
The employer must obtain a certified Labor Condition Application (LCA) before filing Form I-129
If subject to the annual cap, registration must be selected before a full petition can be filed that season
denialReasons: Employer cannot show the role is a specialty occupation
Degree or experience does not relate closely enough to the offered duties
Wage, LCA, or worksite inconsistencies undermine the filing
Support letter and petition evidence tell different stories
Consular concerns about prior immigration history or incomplete interview documentation
commonMistakes: Assuming any college degree automatically fits every job title
Using a vague job description that fails to prove specialty need
Missing registration windows or misunderstanding cap-exempt employers
Starting work before status or stamping authorizes employment
Relying on marketing titles instead of true day-to-day duties

processSteps.title: Confirm role, wage, and specialty fit
processSteps.description: Employer and counsel map duties to specialty criteria, choose the right occupational classification, and confirm required wage for each worksite.

processSteps.title: Complete cap registration if required
processSteps.description: For cap-subject cases, the employer registers during the designated USCIS window. Only selected registrations may file a full petition for that season.

processSteps.title: File and certify the LCA
processSteps.description: Employer submits Form ETA-9035/9035E and completes required notice posting. The certified LCA must match the petitioned role and location(s).

processSteps.title: File Form I-129 with USCIS
processSteps.description: Employer files the petition with LCA, support letter, degree evidence, and fees. Premium processing may be available for faster adjudication.
processSteps.timeframe: Depends on selection and start-date strategy

processSteps.title: Respond to any RFE
processSteps.description: If USCIS requests more evidence, respond with specialty proof, wage documentation, or degree evaluations matching the notice.
processSteps.timeframe: Response window on the RFE notice

processSteps.title: Activate status or obtain a visa stamp
processSteps.description: Inside the U.S., status begins on the approval terms. Abroad, complete DS-160 and the consular interview before entry for H-1B employment.

fees.name: Form I-129 base filing fee
fees.note: Confirm the current USCIS fee schedule before filing.

fees.name: ACWIA training fee
fees.note: Depends on employer size; some exempt entities may not owe this fee.

fees.name: Asylum Program Fee (if applicable)
fees.note: Check current USCIS rules for your employer category.

documents.why: Core identity document for petitions and consular processing.
Show you meet the specialty education requirement.
Explains how a foreign degree compares to a U.S. bachelor’s equivalent.
Connects duties to the need for specialized knowledge and your credentials.
Required wage and working-condition attestation attached to the petition.

documents.item: Prior I-94 and I-797 history (if in the U.S.)
documents.why: Shows maintained status for change or extension filings.
Useful when progressive experience supports qualification or role complexity.

timelineText: Cap-subject H-1B cases generally follow the annual registration cycle, with new employment often tied to the fiscal year start (commonly October 1). Regular USCIS processing can take several months; premium processing can shorten the agency decision window when available. Consular appointment and administrative processing times then vary by embassy.
validityPeriod: Initial approval is commonly up to three years, with extensions often possible up to six years total. Limited exceptions may allow time beyond six years when certain employment-based green card steps are underway.
extensionInfo: Employers file extensions on Form I-129, ideally before status expires. H-1B portability may allow continued work after a timely extension or transfer filing if legal conditions are met. Track I-797 and I-94 end dates carefully.
employmentRights: Employment is employer- and petition-specific. You generally may work only for the petitioning employer, or for concurrent employers that each have their own H-1B filing. Material changes in duties or worksite can require amended petitions.
travelRestrictions: Reentry usually requires a valid H-1B visa stamp (with limited exceptions such as certain Canadian applicants), approval evidence, and current employment documents. Avoid traveling while a critical petition is pending unless counsel confirms the risk is acceptable.
importantDeadlines: Do not start H-1B work before status or admission authorizes it
Begin extension planning several months before I-94 expiry
Cap registration windows are short — employers should not wait until the final day
dependentsText: Spouses and unmarried children under 21 may seek H-4 status. Some H-4 spouses may apply for employment authorization if the H-1B principal meets specific AC21-related criteria, such as an approved I-140 or certain extensions beyond the sixth year.

tips.title: Build the timeline backward from your start date
tips.body: Include registration, LCA, USCIS adjudication, and consular waits — then add buffer for RFEs or document delays.

tips.title: Make the specialty story obvious
tips.body: An officer should not have to guess why this role needs a specialty degree. Duties, hiring norms, and your coursework should align cleanly.

tips.title: Keep one source-of-truth packet
tips.body: Store receipts, I-797s, degree evaluations, and job letters together. You will reuse them for travel, extensions, and transfers.

didYouKnow: Certain cap-exempt employers — including many universities and related research organizations — may file year-round without the lottery.
H-1B is generally treated as dual intent, so pursuing a green card is not automatically inconsistent with the status.

faqs.question: How long can I stay in H-1B status?
faqs.answer: Most people are limited to six years total, often through an initial period plus extensions. Limited exceptions can allow more time when qualifying green card steps are pending or approved.

faqs.question: Can I change H-1B employers?
faqs.answer: Yes. The new employer files a transfer petition. In qualifying cases, portability rules may let you start work once a non-frivolous transfer petition is filed.

faqs.question: What is the H-1B lottery?
faqs.answer: When registrations exceed the annual numerical limit, USCIS randomly selects which registrations may file full petitions. Selection is not the same as petition approval.

faqs.question: Is an H-1B LCA the same as PERM?
faqs.answer: No. The LCA supports temporary H-1B employment. PERM labor certification is a separate process used in many employment-based green card cases.

faqs.question: Can my spouse work on H-4?
faqs.answer: Only in specific situations. Certain H-4 spouses may file Form I-765 when the H-1B holder meets AC21 criteria. Ordinary H-4 status alone does not authorize employment.

relatedWhen.when: Choose L-1 if you are transferring within the same multinational after qualifying foreign employment.
Choose TN if you are a Canadian or Mexican professional in a listed USMCA occupation and need a non-lottery option.
Use OPT when you are an F-1 graduate gaining practical training before an H-1B transition.
Choose F-1 if full-time study, not specialty employment, is the purpose of your stay.
